idiom_name: one-line infix andThen extension or let-chains with function references
implementation_notes: Function types `(A) -> B` are first-class values and lambdas are function literals (kotlinlang.org), but kotlin-stdlib ships no composition combinator - andThen was requested in the Kotlin forums and never landed - so the idiomatic realizations are a one-line infix extension on function types, `infix fun <A, B, C> ((A) -> B).andThen(g: (B) -> C): (A) -> C = { g(this(it)) }`, or chaining scope functions with function references at the call site (`raw.let(::normalize).let(::digest)`); arrow-core's andThen is the library option for codebases already on Arrow. The extension is justified when the chain must be a named reusable value; the let/run chain reads better for a one-shot flow.
pitfalls: let returns the lambda result while also and apply return the receiver, so mixing them into a transformation chain silently forwards the original value to the next step.

Receiver-based function types (String.() -> Int) and plain ones ((String) -> Int) interoperate as values but the receiver form drops out of inference in longer chains, producing confusing errors inside the extension.
With no combinator in the standard library every module that wants one defines its own; two local andThen implementations with different argument order reintroduce the direction bug.
